newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Mar 10.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Mar 10.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Twenty five-year-old Scotsman David Coulthard won yesterday's Australian Grand Prix, giving the first win in three years to the McLaren-Mercedes team after a first-corner tangle eliminated race favourite Jacques Villeneuve. Page 25.

Sydney United soccer striker Ante Milicic last night grabbed a brace of goals in the match against West Adelaide, which Sydney won 4-0, enabling the Pumas to extend their lead at the top of the Ericsson Cup championship table. Page 26.

In a decision released yesterday, NSW cricket captain Greg Matthews has been found guilty of dissent by Australian Cricket Board commissioner Vic Fisher for disputing an umpire's decision. This adds to the NSW Blues' misfortune after they were crushed by Sheffield Shield leaders WA in Perth on Saturday. Page 27.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Despite the an eight point lead held by South-Queensland within the first 25 minutes of its match against the Sydney City Roosters, the Roosters ended up winning by 34-10 at the Sydney Football Stadium. Page 26.

Cronulla Super League coach John Lang has ordered late fitness tests for Danny Lee and Jason Stephens before he decides the line-up for tonight's match against Canterbury. Lang maintains he will only include players if they are capable of carrying out th job, with both teams regarded as particularly aggressive. Page 27.

Despite remarkable displays of support for the ARL at Parramatta Stadium and Leichhardt Oval, Super League chief executive John Ribot last night refused to admit the original competition has established itself as the Sydney market leader. Page 27.
THE AGE

Following muscle spasms in his back that ruled him out of the provincial match against Border, Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor has only been given a 50/50 chance of being fit for the second Test against South Africa on Friday. According to team phsiotherapist Errol Alcott, they wont be able to tell if Taylor can play until Wednesday. Page 2.

Holden Commodore teammates Russell Ingall and Larry Perkins have achieved another one-two finish in the five-litre class at Albert Park on Sunday, completing a perfect lead-up to the opening of the Australian touring car championship. Page 11.

The Sydney Swans AFL team defeated the Western Bulldogs in Ballarat yesterday by 50 points, with both Daniel Hargraves and Jason Watts kicking five goals. With 12 Sydney players sidelined due to injury, coach Rodney Eade used three supplementary players,but he was particularly pleased with the match's outcome. Page 16.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian pole vault world record holder Emma George made it through to the finals of the world indoor championships in Paris yesterday. George's performance raised controversy after she appeared to want to opt out of the competition without needing to clear 4.10 metres. Another Australian medal prospect, Tim Forsyth, failed to reach the high jump finals after only clearing a disappointing 2.24 metres. Page 86.

Speed hitting Australian tennis player Mark Philippoussis will face American Richey Reneberg today in the final of the Arizona Tennis Classic. Philippoussis enjoyed a 4-6 7-6 6-2 semi-final victory yesterday after he rocketed 19 aces past American Chris Woodruff. Page 86.

Australian soccer team Collingwood Warriors is in with a chance to make the Ericsson Cup finals after pulling out of the competition a month ago. Despite winning its third game in succession after beating the Canberra Cosmos 6-2 in the highest scoring mach of the year, Collingwood is almost certain to be axed from the competition at the end of the season. Page 80.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Negotiations are on between the New South Wales Government and the Department of Immigration over the possibility of using the Villawood migrant hostel, currently used to hold suspected illegal immigrants, to accommodate 1500 timekeepers, judges and event officials for the Sydney 2000 Olympics. Page 3.

Unless changes are made to advertising rules on clothing worn during competition, Australian world title holder triathlete Greg Welch will be unable to compete in the prestigious ITU World Cup - the competition that determines athletes' world rankings in he lead-up to the Sydney 2000 Olympic Games. Page 28.

Australian 33-year old Olympic bronze medallist Bruce Hick yesterday won the lightweight double scull at the national rowing selection regatta in Penrith. Hick competed with Gary Lynagh, his partner in a hat-trick of world championships from 1991-93. Page 32.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
